name: Alliance of Independent Social Democrats
summary:
The Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SSDS, Szövetség a Független Szociáldemokratákért) was a post-communist Hungarian political party that emerged in the fragmented political landscape of Hungary's 1989-1990 democratic transition — representing one of many short-lived centrist and social democratic parties that attempted to fill the space between the Hungarian Socialist Party (the reformed communist party) and the various conservative and nationalist parties that dominated Hungary's first free elections.

Hungary's 1990 democratic transition was one of the most peaceful and negotiated of the Eastern European revolutions of 1989: the Hungarian Socialist Workers' Party (communist) had been reforming itself since 1988, and the 'Negotiated Transition' (Kerekasztal Tárgyalások, Round Table Negotiations) between the communist government and opposition groups produced a remarkably orderly transition. This negotiated character of Hungarian democratization meant that the political landscape was more complex than in countries with more dramatic revolutionary breaks.

The Alliance of Independent Social Democrats, like many small centrist parties in Hungary's early democratic period, attempted to occupy the center-left space but faced competition from both the reformed Hungarian Socialist Party and the various new democratic parties. Most such small centrist parties either merged with larger organizations or disappeared in subsequent elections as Hungary's party system consolidated around fewer, larger parties.
